why: The row is mostly definitions (FourTermExact, Choice, Choice.value, canonicalChoice, phi, phiEquiv); its only theorem, A = phi_ne_zero (Φ_E ≠ 0), is equivalent to B's clause (3) (Φ_E bijective) because both sides are lines: a nonzero map of lines is bijective, an injective map out of a line is nonzero. B's clauses (1) (the four wedges of every blind choice are nonzero) and (2) (Φ_E satisfies (91) for some choice) are about the definitions, not about A's theorem; they were proved from the definitions with non-item lemmas: a blind choice maps to a project Choice with literally the same wedges (rfl), so wedgeB_ne_zero / wedgeC_ne_zero / wedge_basis_ne_zero give (1), and phi is by definition smulRight (dualVec source) value for canonicalChoice, which with eq_dualVec_of_apply_eq_one gives (2) for the canonical choice. Lemma 6.5 (for every choice, item V6_6) was not needed. So the project's definition of Φ_E is the text's (91) made with one choice, and A adds only Φ_E ≠ 0.
